operations.evidence: The Home Office release was published on 22 July 2026 and reports police workforce statistics as at 31 March 2026 for England and Wales.
The publication is a workforce snapshot and does not measure incidents or risk at an individual parcel.
The release covers the 43 territorial police forces in England and Wales and reports British Transport Police figures separately.
Force-area workforce coverage is not exact-address or parcel-level evidence.
The release covers police officers, police staff, designated officers, PCSOs, special constables and police support volunteers.
Worker counts describe organisational capacity rather than local incident exposure.
There were 234,441 FTE paid police workers in the 43 territorial forces as at 31 March 2026.
A national workforce total cannot identify conditions around a particular property.
The total paid workforce decreased by 1,332 FTE, or 0.6%, compared with March 2025.
A year-on-year staffing change is not a parcel-level public-safety score.
The March 2026 total workforce was 10,056 FTE, or 4.1%, below the March 2010 peak.
A historical staffing comparison does not establish local causation or risk.
There were 145,886 FTE police officers in the 43 territorial forces as at 31 March 2026.
The figure is an aggregate headcount-equivalent measure and cannot be assigned to a parcel.
Police officer numbers decreased by 566 FTE, or 0.4%, compared with March 2025.
National workforce movement cannot substitute for local incident data.
Police officer numbers were 1,859 FTE, or 1.3%, below the March 2024 peak.
A gap from a national peak is not evidence about a neighbourhood or address.
British Transport Police employed 2,817 FTE police officers in England and Wales as at 31 March 2026.
BTP staffing is reported separately and cannot be attributed to a land parcel.
The release reports 5,540 FTE National Crime Agency officers in England and Wales.
NCA staffing is not a measure of crime prevalence around a property.
There were 350 FTE police officers seconded to central services.
Secondment totals are organisational data, not geographic public-safety evidence.
There were 5,196 special constables on a headcount basis in the 43 territorial forces.
Special constable headcount has no contracted-hours denominator and is not parcel evidence.
There were 6,035 police support volunteers on a headcount basis in the 43 territorial forces.
Volunteer headcount does not indicate service intensity or local incident risk.
There were 81,296 FTE police staff and designated officers as at 31 March 2026.
Staffing levels are organisational aggregates and cannot score a parcel.
Police staff and designated officer numbers decreased by 710 FTE, or 0.9%, from March 2025.
Annual staffing change does not establish local service availability at an address.
Police staff and designated officer numbers were 2,140 FTE, or 2.6%, below the March 2010 peak.
Historical national comparison is not a local risk measure.
There were 7,259 FTE PCSOs as at 31 March 2026.
PCSO totals are not neighbourhood incident counts and cannot be parcel-attributed.
PCSO numbers decreased by 55 FTE, or 0.8%, compared with March 2025.
A national change does not describe conditions at a specific location.
PCSO numbers were 9,658 FTE, or 57.1%, below the March 2010 peak.
A long-term workforce gap cannot be converted into an address-level safety score.
Special constable headcount decreased by 324, or 5.9%, compared with March 2025.
The change is a national workforce statistic, not parcel evidence.
As at 31 March 2026, 90.5% of police officers were recorded in frontline roles.
Frontline classification is based on primary role and does not measure all activity around a parcel.
There were 115,764 FTE police officers recorded in frontline roles as at 31 March 2026.
A national frontline total cannot establish local response capacity for an exact address.
Frontline officer numbers decreased by 1,518 FTE, or 1.3%, from March 2025.
National year-on-year change is not a parcel-specific service metric.
The March 2026 frontline total was 7,701 FTE below the March 2023 peak.
A workforce peak comparison cannot be used as direct local-risk evidence.
There were 55,561 FTE officers in Local policing roles, accounting for 43.4% of officers.
Function allocation reflects primary duties and cannot identify coverage at one parcel.
There were 23,676 FTE officers in Investigations roles, accounting for 18.5% of officers.
Investigation staffing is not a local crime or response-time measure.
Functions statistics classify workers by the primary role in which they spend most of their time.
The classification may omit secondary duties and must not be overinterpreted for parcel scoring.
Functions data from 2015 onward use the CIPFA Police Objective Analysis framework and are not directly comparable with the earlier framework.
Framework changes limit long-run comparisons and prevent unqualified local inference.
Guidance clarified that student officers in classroom-based training should be recorded in the Other function group.
The recording change affects comparability and does not reflect a sudden local operational change.
